about.title: A steadier way forward, built around people.
about.description: We are a fictional community-minded bank created for this demo project. Our story is about making everyday money decisions feel more understandable and less stressful.
about.story: Westbridge began with a straightforward idea: banking should help people move forward, not make them work harder to understand their options. We bring clear information, useful digital tools, and human support together in one place.
about.mission: Make everyday banking clearer, more accessible, and more supportive for the people and businesses we serve.

scamTips: Never share a one-time passcode, password, or full card details in response to an unexpected call or message.
Pause before opening links. Visit the official site or app directly instead of using a link in a surprise message.
Be cautious of urgent requests to move money, buy gift cards, or keep a transaction secret.
Verify a caller independently using a trusted number, not a number they provide during the call.
Report suspicious activity promptly and freeze your card if you believe it may be compromised.

items.question: How quickly can I open an account?
items.answer: Most applicants can complete the initial setup in under ten minutes, with access available after verification.

items.question: What do I need to open an account?
items.answer: You will need basic personal details and identity information. The demo does not collect or store real financial data.

items.question: Can I open more than one account?
items.answer: Yes. You can organize everyday spending and savings in separate accounts for different goals.

items.question: Can I send money to friends and family?
items.answer: Instant transfers and scheduled payments are available for supported account types in this demo experience.

items.question: How do I protect my card if it goes missing?
items.answer: Pause or freeze a card in the app, then reactivate it if you find it.

items.question: What are the daily transaction limits?
items.answer: Limits vary by activity type. The interface should show applicable limits before a transfer is submitted.

items.question: Can I set alerts for card purchases?
items.answer: Yes. Account notifications help you stay aware of recent card activity.

items.question: Can I set savings goals?
items.answer: Create a goal, schedule transfers, and review your progress from your account dashboard.

items.question: How do I estimate a loan payment?
items.answer: Use the loan calculator on our loans page to model an estimated payment based on amount, rate, and term.

items.question: Are the rates on this site current offers?
items.answer: No. Rates shown are illustrative demo data only and are not actual offers.

items.question: What support hours are available?
items.answer: Support is presented as available around the clock for account and security questions in this fictional demo.

items.question: How does Westbridge protect my information?
items.answer: The demo describes measures such as encryption, multi-factor verification, and account alerts.

items.question: What should I do if I receive a suspicious message?
items.answer: Do not share codes or follow unexpected links. Contact support using the official site or app.

blog.title: Building a better savings routine without overspending
blog.excerpt: A simple monthly rhythm can help you save with less friction and more consistency.
paragraphs: A savings routine works best when it fits your real life. Start by choosing a repeatable amount that leaves room for bills, essentials, and a little flexibility.
Next, connect the habit to a moment that already happens each month, such as payday. An automatic transfer can make progress feel steady without requiring constant attention.
Finally, give each goal a name and check in occasionally. The point is not to optimize every dollar; it is to make the next good decision easier to repeat.

blog.title: When to review your loan before rates change again
blog.excerpt: Small differences in rate and term can shift your monthly budget in meaningful ways.
paragraphs: Reviewing a loan is less about chasing a headline rate and more about checking whether the full arrangement still fits your plans.
Compare the current balance, remaining term, any fees, and the total cost of a new option. A lower monthly payment can still mean paying more overall if the term is extended.
Use estimates as a starting point, then ask a qualified professional to explain the details before making a decision. Figures on this demo site are illustrative only.

blog.title: Three money habits that make the first year of homeownership calmer
blog.excerpt: A steady system for bills, savings, and emergencies helps reduce stress when life gets busy.
paragraphs: The first year in a new home often brings expenses that are easy to overlook. A monthly review of upcoming bills can help keep those costs visible.
A separate home-maintenance savings goal creates room for repairs and seasonal needs. Even small, regular contributions can make the next unexpected expense easier to absorb.
Keep the system simple: automate what you can, review it once a month, and adjust when your circumstances change. There is no single budget that works for everyone.

sections.heading: Information in this demo
sections.body: This is a fictional educational project. Do not enter real personal, account, or financial information. Form submissions are mocked in the client and are not sent to a banking service.

sections.heading: How information could be used

sections.heading: Your choices

sections.heading: Questions

sections.heading: No real accounts or offers
